title: Oropharyngeal microbiome analyses in newborns in connection with the oropharyngeal application of colostrum
summary:
To find out how the administration of colostrum (the first breast milk) affects the development of the bacterial community in the mouth and throat (oropharyngeal microbiome) of newborns, we take saliva samples at three fixed times:

- Before the first colostrum administration
- The day after the first feed
- On the third day of life or the third day after colostrum administration

The samples are taken as part of routine aspiration. We want to investigate how the microbiome in the mouth and throat - and possibly also in the lungs - changes as a result of colostrum administration. We are not only interested in which bacteria are generally present, but also whether certain types of bacteria colonize more and whether genes responsible for the production of natural substances are activated.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Existing oropharyngeal feeding
- Written declaration of consent from the legal guardians after a detailed, personal discussion and inspection of the parental information sheet.
- Newborns born after the 30th week of pregnancy
- Children who do not receive colostrum but only formula food (control group)
Exclusion criteria:
- Newborns who receive colostrum exclusively via a stomach tube.
- Colostrum administration before the first sample collection
- Newborns who receive donated (pooled) breast milk
- Severe malformations of the thorax, abdomen or internal organs
- Chromosomal aberrations
- sepsis and/or relevantly impaired general condition.
